response: This is just another blow against democracy from South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden, who signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday to force new registered voters to prove they are United States citizens before they can cast a ballot in state elections. The press release claims it only applies to state elections and only impacts new registrants, but this is plainly a structural attack on voting access meant to entrench inequality and keep power in the hands of those who already hold it. By piling on proof requirements, the bill will hit hardest on vulnerable groups like immigrants, working people, and communities of color who already face systemic barriers to documentation, all in service of maintaining historical patterns of exclusion rather than expanding rights for everyone. We cannot let these kinds of institutional moves go unchallenged if we care about real justice and reform.
